bofa-estimates-ai-hyperscaler-capex-appr.headline: BofA estimates AI hyperscaler CapEx approaching $800bn in 2026 (+67% YoY), trending toward $1 trillion in 2027; capex-vs-revenue gap concern intensifying
bofa-estimates-ai-hyperscaler-capex-appr.summary: The IMF's October 13 World Economic Outlook (released at Bangkok Annual Meetings) explicitly flagged AI-investment borrowing by technology firms as compounding advanced-economy benchmark yield pressure, with public debt in advanced economies projected to reach 115% of GDP by 2031 from 108% in 2025; the GFSR (also released October 13) is expected to quantify AI capex debt risks in financial stability terms.
bofa-estimates-ai-hyperscaler-capex-appr.target_indicator: AI capex-vs-revenue gap concern (0 closing / 1 wide / 2 widening fast)
bofa-estimates-ai-hyperscaler-capex-appr.rationale: The IMF's explicit call-out of AI-investment borrowing as a source of advanced-economy yield pressure — at the flagship WEO level — is a material policy signal for s8_ai_capex. The AI capex-vs-revenue gap concern indicator should move toward '2 widening fast' given multilateral institutional recognition of the risk. This is not a new story but a significant escalation in the official narrative around an existing tracked risk.

boj-officials-signal-rate-hikes-every-fe.headline: BOJ officials signal rate hikes every few months; 30yr JGB yields at 3.88%, 10yr at 2.61% — carry trade unwind risk acute
boj-officials-signal-rate-hikes-every-fe.summary: Japan's 30-year JGB yield reached a Ministry of Finance series high of 4.166% on October 5 before settling at 4.04% on October 13; the 10-year is at 3.02%, up 132 bps year-on-year. The US–Japan 30-year spread has compressed to ~120 bps, eroding the risk-adjusted carry on leveraged short-yen positions to an estimated 2.1% annualised vs. 6.4% in early 2024.
boj-officials-signal-rate-hikes-every-fe.rationale: The 30-year JGB yield is a direct tracker indicator for s2_japan. At 4.04%—a series record—and with the US–Japan 30-year spread compressed to ~120 bps (from ~360 bps at start-2025), the fiscal and carry-trade channels are simultaneously under pressure. An estimated $280 bn of leveraged short-yen offshore positions remain; the August 2024 VaR shock analogue is now live again. This is the single most material development of the week and warrants an immediate indicator update and elevated alert on s2_japan.

china-s-nov-2026-extraterritorial-rare-e.headline: China's Nov-2026 extraterritorial rare-earth enforcement deadline is 4 months away; aerospace yttrium shortages already reported
china-s-nov-2026-extraterritorial-rare-e.summary: Following the Trump-Xi summit in Washington in late September 2026, China extended its one-year suspension of the expanded rare-earth export controls (originally due to expire November 10, 2026) until January 10, 2027, with no jointly documented critical-minerals settlement; the April 2025 controls on seven heavy REEs remain fully active, and the blacklist of 10 US and 14 EU firms imposed in June-July 2026 (including MP Materials and USA Rare Earth) was not lifted.
china-s-nov-2026-extraterritorial-rare-e.target_indicator: Nov-2025 pause status (0 extended / 1 expiring / 2 lapsed)
china-s-nov-2026-extraterritorial-rare-e.rationale: The pause status indicator for s6_rare_earths must be updated: the November 2026 expiry date has shifted to January 10, 2027, meaning the indicator moves from '1 expiring' back to '0 extended' — but only by 60 days and without a formal deal. Critically, the US domestic RE producer blacklist indicator should move to '1 entity-specific ban' given the June 2026 MOFCOM actions against MP Materials and USA Rare Earth. These are high-materiality changes to two existing indicators in the same story.

japan-10-year-jgb-yield-surges-to-2-7-2-.headline: Japan 10-Year JGB Yield Surges to ~2.7–2.8% (30-Year High), Yen Near 4-Decade Low; BOJ Hikes to 1%
japan-10-year-jgb-yield-surges-to-2-7-2-.summary: PM Takaichi's ¥10 trillion two-year consumption-tax cut is scheduled for submission to parliament in mid-October, but funding clarity remains elusive: the government pledged to avoid deficit-financing bonds yet has not identified an alternative revenue source. Oxford Economics has raised its end-2026 10Y JGB forecast to 2.8%; actual 10Y yields have already blown through that to 3.02% on Oct 12, with 30Y at 4.06%, pressuring carry-trade unwinds and JGB market functioning amid BoJ QT.
japan-10-year-jgb-yield-surges-to-2-7-2-.target_indicator: 30-year JGB yield (%) AND Takaichi plan financing clarity (0 ok / 1 unclear / 2 disorderly)
japan-10-year-jgb-yield-surges-to-2-7-2-.rationale: 30Y JGB is at 4.06% (data from Oct 12 Trading Economics), well above any prior tracker levels. The Takaichi financing-clarity indicator should move from 1 (unclear) toward 2 (disorderly): the mid-October bill submission without a credible funding mechanism was flagged explicitly by MUFG Research as 'a critical test.' Trump administration pressure on Japan's fiscal stance (noted by MUFG) adds an external layer. Both existing s2 indicators need immediate updates.

japan-us-coordinated-fx-intervention-jul.headline: Japan–US coordinated FX intervention July 31: structural yen weakness unresolved as BOJ faces fiscal-monetary trilemma
japan-us-coordinated-fx-intervention-jul.summary: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate 25bps to 1.25% in a split 7-2 decision on September 18, citing upside inflation risk, taking rates to their highest since 1995. The yen remains near 156-157 post-intervention (Japan and US conducted coordinated yen-buying in late July), while the 10-yr JGB yield sits at ~3.10% and the 30-yr at ~4.04%, with the curve reflecting both BOJ tightening trajectory and unresolved Takaichi fiscal risk premium.

proposed_indicator.label: US-Japan coordinated FX intervention flag (0 none / 1 unilateral BoJ / 2 joint US-Japan)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = no intervention; 1 = BoJ acting alone (standard); 2 = joint US Treasury + BoJ intervention signaling systemic yen stress. Current reading: 2. Reset to 1 when joint action ceases; to 0 after 90 days of market stability.

japan-us-coordinated-fx-intervention-jul.rationale: The US-Japan coordinated FX intervention in late July is a qualitative escalation not captured by the current USD/JPY level indicator alone. Coordinated intervention signals a geopolitical dimension to yen management (Treasury Secretary Bessent publicly confirmed US involvement), changing the risk topology: it creates a de facto floor but also a political tripwire if the yen depreciates past it again. This gap in the indicator set matters for carry-unwind risk assessment.

us-treasury-emergency-long-bond-buybacks.headline: US Treasury emergency long-bond buybacks send gold to ~$4,719/oz; dollar index at 3-month lows — de-dollarization safe-haven dynamic intensifying
us-treasury-emergency-long-bond-buybacks.summary: Gold is trading at approximately $4,157–4,182/oz on October 13, more than 20% below the January 28, 2026 record high (estimated $5,420–5,595/oz), as the World Gold Council revised Q1 2026 central bank purchases sharply down from 244 tonnes to 56.5 tonnes. The correction calls into question the structural central-bank-demand pillar that drove the 2025 rally.
us-treasury-emergency-long-bond-buybacks.rationale: Gold price is a direct indicator for s12_gold_dedollar. A >20% decline from an all-time record, combined with a World Gold Council data revision showing central bank buying collapsed from 244 to 56.5 tonnes in Q1 2026, is material: the de-dollarization narrative was predicated partly on sustained EM central bank accumulation. A sharp reversal in that demand pillar, combined with gold still elevated in absolute terms (~$4,157), suggests the 'Reserve-weaponization / settlement shift' indicator may need re-assessment—the structural shift is continuing but the velocity of demand has stalled, a nuance not captured by the existing band indicator.

synchronized-global-sovereign-bond-rout-.headline: Synchronized global sovereign bond rout: US 10y at 4.80%, UK 30y at 5.82% (highest since 1998), German 10y at 2011 highs
synchronized-global-sovereign-bond-rout-.summary: The 10-year OAT–Bund spread touched 146.9 bps on October 2 and remained at 139.5 bps on October 12, as France's National Assembly opened budget debate on October 13 targeting a still-wide 5% of GDP deficit in 2027. Moody's sovereign review is scheduled for October 23; a downgrade would push French banks—large holders of domestic sovereign debt—into further stress.
synchronized-global-sovereign-bond-rout-.rationale: OAT–Bund spread and Rating action are both direct tracker indicators for s10_france. The spread at 139.5–146.9 bps is at a 15-year extreme, and an imminent Moody's review on Oct 23 creates a binary event risk that directly maps to the 'Rating action' indicator (currently 1-negative outlook, risk of flipping to 2-downgrade). The budget debate also touches 'Govt stability' (Article 49.3 risk). All three s10_france indicators are simultaneously elevated, making this the highest-urgency eurozone item of the week.

strait-of-hormuz-remains-contested-brent.headline: Strait of Hormuz remains contested: Brent hit $114/bbl in September; EIA forecasts $105/bbl Q4 2026; Saudi East-West pipeline attacked
strait-of-hormuz-remains-contested-brent.summary: EIA's October 6 STEO reports Brent averaged $114/bbl in September after attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline temporarily halted the key Hormuz bypass route; crude shut-ins are still estimated at 4.5 mb/d in Q4 2026. Simultaneously, the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement was invoked for the first time in October 2026 following fresh Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure, threatening to widen the conflict to the Red Sea corridor as well.

proposed_indicator.label: Middle East crude shut-in volume (mb/d, EIA estimate)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = <1 mb/d (normal); 1 = 1–4 mb/d (disrupted); 2 = >4 mb/d (severe, as now at 4.5 mb/d)

strait-of-hormuz-remains-contested-brent.rationale: s20_sea_lanes tracks Hormuz/Red Sea status as an ordinal 0/1/2 flag and WTI crude price, but has no indicator capturing the physical volume of supply knocked offline. With 4.5 mb/d still shut-in in Q4 2026 — the largest sustained disruption in history per the World Bank — the existing binary status flag is insufficient granularity. The pipeline attack also opens a new bypass-route vulnerability that the existing rubric does not address. Adding a mb/d shut-in indicator would give the tracker a continuous, source-able signal tied directly to EIA's monthly STEO.

mecca-joint-defense-agreement-invoked-fo.headline: Mecca Joint Defense Agreement invoked for first time (October 2026) after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
mecca-joint-defense-agreement-invoked-fo.summary: The trilateral Mecca Joint Defense Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey was invoked for the first time in October 2026 following a series of Houthi drone and missile strikes on Saudi infrastructure. Yemen's internationally recognized government simultaneously launched 'Operation Dawn of Yemen', a large-scale counteroffensive targeting Houthi-held Red Sea coastal territory, risking further escalation of a second maritime chokepoint.

proposed_story.name: Gulf War Spillover — Regional Coalition Escalation Risk
proposed_story.why: The invocation of the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement introduces a multi-state military alliance dynamic not captured by any existing story. If Pakistan (a nuclear state) becomes operationally entangled alongside Saudi Arabia and Turkey against Houthi-Iranian forces, the conflict crosses a systemic threshold: it is no longer a bilateral US-Israel-Iran war but a regional coalition war with nuclear overhang, direct implications for Pakistan's fiscal stability (IMF program), and cascading effects on LNG/oil routes, food/fertilizer supply chains (Pakistani wheat imports), and EM sovereign spreads. None of s20_sea_lanes, s18_food_fertilizer, or s4_dev_debt individually captures a nuclear-armed state's entry into the conflict as a formal co-belligerent.

indicators.label: Mecca JDA activation status (0 = dormant / 1 = invoked-non-kinetic / 2 = kinetic coalition operations)
indicators.rubric: 0 = agreement not activated; 1 = invoked for diplomatic/logistical support (current); 2 = Pakistani or Turkish forces engaged in active combat operations

indicators.label: Pakistan sovereign CDS 5Y (bps)
indicators.rubric: Rising spread signals market pricing of fiscal/conflict stress on the nuclear-armed coalition partner; threshold >800 bps = high alert

indicators.label: Red Sea container transit volume (% of pre-crisis baseline)

mecca-joint-defense-agreement-invoked-fo.rationale: The first-ever invocation of a formal multilateral defense treaty in response to the Iran war is a qualitative escalation that no existing story tracks. It introduces Pakistan (nuclear state, IMF program country, large wheat importer) as a potential direct participant, creates a new military-alliance feedback loop, and threatens to transform the Red Sea from a contested to a fully blocked chokepoint. This materially affects s4_dev_debt, s18_food_fertilizer, and s20_sea_lanes simultaneously, warranting its own story node.

imf-weo-bangkok-oct-13-global-public-deb.headline: IMF WEO Bangkok (Oct 13): global public debt near post-WWII highs; developing nations face $400bn external payments in 2026
imf-weo-bangkok-oct-13-global-public-deb.summary: The IMF's October 2026 WEO, released in Bangkok today, warns that global public debt is at its highest since World War II and will exceed 100% of GDP before 2030; developing countries collectively face $400bn in external debt payments this year, with interest already exceeding 10% of revenue on average. The Fund explicitly flagged that energy-importer EMDEs are being squeezed simultaneously by $96/bbl average oil prices and high refinancing costs.

proposed_indicator.label: EM external debt service pressure index (IMF/World Bank: 0 = manageable / 1 = rising / 2 = cluster of missed payments or restructurings)
proposed_indicator.rubric: Combines: (a) share of EMDEs with interest>10% of revenue, (b) new IMF emergency programs activated in past 90 days, (c) missed coupon events. Score 2 if $400bn+ in annual payments coincides with commodity shock — current reading is '2'.

imf-weo-bangkok-oct-13-global-public-deb.rationale: s4_dev_debt already tracks the US dollar index, US 10Y real yield, and a qualitative IMF-programs indicator. The IMF's Bangkok data point — $400bn external payments wall for developing nations, interest >10% of revenue on average, post-WWII debt levels — is a material new quantification of the stress that the existing IMF-programs indicator only partially captures. A formal 'EM external debt service pressure index' would give the tracker a forward-looking, IMF-sourced composite that fires before missed coupons appear in headlines.
